title: THE VISSION weekly review
description: A once-a-week synthesis of the paper's OWN continuity fields — threads, open questions and corrections — over the trailing 7 calendar days ending at the latest published edition. No model, no new research: every string here is either copied verbatim from a field an edition already published (thread.label, openQuestion, resolves.outcome, corrections[].what) or a fixed template with a computed count substituted in. There is no url or free-text-citation field anywhere in this schema — the only pointer type is a storyId matching edition.schema.json's own permalink pattern, which is what makes 'this cannot introduce a new sourcing risk' a property of the schema rather than a promise about a generator. See tools/weekly.mjs.

date.description: The filename stem — the date this review was generated, not a claim about the news. Wall-clock at generation time, same convention as digest.edition.date.

from.description: = latest included edition date minus 6 days. Computed with the same arithmetic as build.mjs's topicOfTheWeek (setUTCDate, never new Date() against the wall clock) so the two can never silently disagree about what 'this week' means.

to.description: The latest published edition date on or before this review's own generation date. Never the wall clock.

editionDates.description: The editions that actually fell inside [from, to]. Can be 1, or several — never assumed to be 7. This archive has real multi-day gaps between editions, and padding this to look like a full week would be inventing a publishing cadence that didn't happen.

stats.description: Plain counts of the paper's own output in the window — the one kind of number this page may state without a per-story citation, because 'N stories ran across M editions' is checkable by counting. A claim about the news itself is not.

generator.description: Deliberately no "model" key, unlike edition.generator — v1 of this pipeline calls no model at all.

threads.description: The FULL standing list of every thread this archive has ever declared, not just ones that moved this week — a quiet week still shows the whole scoreboard rather than an empty section. Threads with no instalment inside the window simply carry an empty instalmentsThisWeek.

stillOpen.description: The FULL standing ledger of every question this archive has ever asked and never answered — not windowed. This is what lets the page function as a scoreboard ('N questions remain open') even in a week where nothing moved.

corrections.description: Windowed on the correction's OWN `at` timestamp, never on the edition date of the story it corrects — a correction can land on a story published several editions earlier, and this archive already has exactly that case.

storyId.description: Must match an id that exists somewhere in the full archive. tools/weekly.mjs refuses to write the file if any story id here does not resolve — a referential check this codebase has nowhere else.

label.description: Copied verbatim from the thread's newest instalment — never rewritten here.

openedAt.description: The edition date of the thread's first instalment.

outcome.description: Copied verbatim from the answering story's resolves.outcome — including when it shows the desk was wrong. That is the entire value of the mechanism (CLAUDE.md).

afterDays.description: daysBetween(askedAt, answeredAt) — reused from tools/lib/continuity.mjs so this number can never drift from open-questions.html's own.

daysOpen.description: daysBetween(askedAt, latest published edition date) — the SAME reference point open-questions.html itself uses (build.mjs's renderOpenQuestions reads `today` as editions[0].edition.date, never the wall clock), so this number matches that page exactly rather than drifting because the weekly happened to run on a different day.

editionDate.description: The ORIGINAL story's edition date — can be well before this week's window, since a correction is windowed on when it was made, not on when the story ran.

at.description: Copied verbatim from the correction's own timestamp. This is what the window is filtered on.
